punchline: Brooks's remedy for a late project is not more people, because 50 people create 1,225 possible conversations.
thirty_sec: IBM's boss reportedly asked Fred Brooks, in his exit interview, why software was so much harder to manage than hardware. Brooks had run OS/360 and had added programmers to a project that was already late, which made it later. His answer became Brooks's law. The reason is arithmetic: every pair of people is a channel, so ten people have 45 and fifty have 1,225.
